clue.text: A seventh rather flat sporting representative going on record

indicators.note: one piece going on after another signals that they are joined in sequence

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University at a sport
to note something is to record it

explanation.surface: A sporting representative's record seems to be a seventh-placed, rather flat showing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a disappointing seventh place; in music it is a flattened seventh. An Oxbridge Blue is a British university sportsman or sportswoman.
explanation.definitionFit: In blues and jazz the characteristic slightly flattened third or seventh degree of the scale carries this name.

clue.text: See 10
Rabbit on the breakfast menu?

definitions.meaning: to rabbit (on) is British slang for talking at tedious length
a battered griddle cake often served at breakfast

explanation.surface: Rabbit appearing at breakfast sounds like an odd dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to talk on vaguely and at length, and a crisp gridded batter cake eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Staggeringly wealthy?

parts.note: someone staggering about drunk is lurching from side to side

explanation.surface: A description of someone fabulously rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggeringly' looks like an intensifier for wealthy, but it describes swaying gait, while the answer completes the idiom 'rolling in it' for the money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both a lurching, swaying walk and, in the idiom about money, being extremely rich.

clue.text: Back massage, skirting large unclear spot

indicators.note: skirting means going around the edge of something, so the reversed letters surround the next piece
back tells us the word for massage is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to rub is to massage
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A back massage that avoids a large, vague patch of skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' attaches to massage as a body part in the surface, but it is the reversal signal turning RUB into BUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge or indistinct patch where nothing is sharply visible is a smeared, out-of-focus spot.

clue.text: Bridge player initially breaking into clubs — I say, hearts overlooked!

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word player is used
breaking means the letters of the word into are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the letter for hearts is dropped from the greeting

parts.note: an exclamation to attract attention, like hello
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A bridge player bursts into a club, exclaiming that hearts were missed.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game surface hides a musical bridge. 'breaking' makes ONTI from INTO, and 'overlooked' drops H from HELLO, leaving the cockney-sounding ELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'little bridge', the term names the bridge of a violin and the instruction to bow close to it.

clue.text: Enjoying a certain 15 minutes of Camus' unopened novel?

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
unopened means the opening letter of the name Camus is removed

explanation.surface: Someone basking in brief celebrity thanks to a novel by Camus they never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the C from CAMUS, and 'novel' rearranges OF with AMUS. The 15 minutes refers to Andy Warhol's line that everyone will be world-renowned for fifteen minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Warhol's 'fifteen minutes of fame' is brief celebrity, so a person enjoying it is, for that time, well known.

clue.text: Road touring date snapped up by rock group — good place to make money

indicators.note: snapped up by means taken inside, so the band's letters close around the rest

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a British rock band

indicators.note: touring suggests travelling about, so the letters of road wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A touring date along the road is grabbed by a rock band, a lucrative gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges ROAD into ORAD. ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, was a 1970s British rock band; the answer is the legendary city of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by Spanish explorers stands for any place where riches can be made.

clue.text: City imports drugs (not ecstasy) as a treatment for shaking

indicators.note: imports means brings inside, so the city's letters hold the next piece

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: not means the following letter is taken away from the drugs word

parts.note: dope is slang for drugs
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A city brings in drugs, though not ecstasy, as a cure for tremors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' points to the tremor of Parkinson's disease; the hyphenated drug name keeps its L as a separate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This amino-acid drug, converted to dopamine in the brain, is the standard medication for Parkinson's tremors.

clue.text: In need of something on top for congestion etc?

definitions.text: In need of something on top
definitions.meaning: a bare, chilly cranium would want a hat on it
a common illness with a blocked nose, sneezing and so on

explanation.surface: A wry hint that someone wants a hat to ward off a stuffy nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means a chilly crown wanting a hat; as an ailment it is a catarrhal infection with blocked sinuses.

clue.text: Straining to airlift bananas at end of season

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of to airlift go mad and rearrange
at end of means the closing letter of the word season is used

explanation.surface: Effort to fly in bananas at the close of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the cargo, but it is the anagram signal for TO AIRLIFT; 'at end of' takes the N from season.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing a liquid through a sieve or filter paper to remove solids is a process of sieving it clean.

clue.text: Bar accommodating one hundred runners at the start

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the bar's letters hold the next ones

parts.note: a pole is a bar or rod
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A bar that has room for a hundred runners on the starting line.
explanation.walkthrough: The race surface misleads: London's first organised force was the Bow Street Runners, founded in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bow Street Runners were early law officers, so the runners of the beginning were the first constabulary.

clue.text: Cares halved at first? Can't decide

indicators.note: at first tells us the halving word comes before the word for cares

parts.note: something halved has been cut in two
to mind is to care, so cares gives minds

explanation.surface: Someone whose worries were cut by half at first, leaving them hesitant.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being torn between two choices and unable to settle, so it means being undecided.

clue.text: Virgin's rejected a factual programme

parts.note: virgin means new, plus the S of the possessive
something cast off or cast aside has been rejected

explanation.surface: Virgin's rejection of a documentary pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin looks like the company name; it is just the adjective meaning untouched or fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast of current events on radio or television is a programme of factual reporting.

clue.text: Question authority

definitions.meaning: an interrogative word asking which person
the World Health Organization, a United Nations health authority

explanation.surface: An instruction to challenge those in power.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the pronoun used to ask about a person, and the initials of the UN body that governs international health.

clue.text: Casually jilted outside entrance to synagogue, Dutch style

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
casually means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters of jilted are thrown into a new order
entrance to means the opening letter of the word synagogue

explanation.surface: Someone casually dumped a partner outside a synagogue door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casually' turns JILTED into DETIJL, which 'outside' wraps around the S from 'entrance to synagogue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The early-20th-century Netherlands art movement of Mondrian, named after its magazine, is a design idiom from Holland.

clue.text: Stuff that's promised for tomorrow?

parts.note: from Lewis Carroll's White Queen, who offers a fruit preserve every other day but never today: a treat always promised, never delivered

explanation.surface: A question about what is being promised for the next day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass the White Queen offers this preserve on alternate days but never today; the phrase now means rewards forever postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit preserve from Carroll's line has become the stock image of a pledge that never arrives.

clue.text: Court getting the king's mistress to return warm wear

parts.note: to court a lover is to woo them

indicators.note: to return means the name of the mistress is read backwards

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A courtier persuades the royal mistress to come back for something warm to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses NELL to LLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments knitted from sheep's fleece are cosy clothing, so the plural noun means knitted warm clothes.

clue.text: Make-up book is in the centre, miss

indicators.note: is in means the book letter sits inside the other letters

parts.note: the eye is the centre, as of a storm or a target
to miss something is to lack it

explanation.surface: A make-up book is at the centre of what a young woman is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' reads as a young woman but is a verb meaning to be without; 'the centre' is the eye of a storm or target.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara or dark cosmetic applied to the lashes and lids is a form of cosmetics.

clue.text: Jacques Tati's film business

definitions.meaning: Tati's 1971 comedy about Monsieur Hulot driving to a car show, released in English under this title
dealing or trade, as in illicit trade in drugs

explanation.surface: The commercial side of Jacques Tati's cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the English title of Tati's motoring comedy and a word for commercial dealing or trade.

clue.text: Singer, performing as well as ever, about to make a comeback

parts.note: a performer at their best is said to be in form

indicators.note: to make a comeback means the word for about is turned back to front

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A singer back at their best, about to return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist, but in criminal slang to sing is to tell tales to the police. 'to make a comeback' reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Underworld slang for confessing or betraying associates to police is singing, so a grass is a singer.

clue.text: Name, or any other group of 9

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters of or any are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: Naming one nine-strong set, or any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' turns OR ANY into ONARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective and noun built on the Latin for nine describe a set of nine or base-nine counting.

clue.text: In earnest, one snatched weights

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone seriously grabbed a weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across earneST ONE Snatched. A stone is a British unit of body weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is a British measure of mass of fourteen pounds, so the plural is units of heaviness.

clue.text: Ostentatious display of band to secure record backing

indicators.note: to secure means to hold firmly, so the band's letters close around the record

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the body

indicators.note: backing means the record's letters go in reverse

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A band makes a show of locking in a record deal for its backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of cloth worn across the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a big showy impression, as in money spent lavishly, is a flamboyant show.

clue.text: Acute and visible sort of flu

parts.note: something that can be seen is in sight

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters of flu are sorted into a different order

explanation.surface: An acute and obvious bout of a kind of influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acute' reads as a medical term for the flu, but it means sharp-witted. 'sort of' rearranges FLU to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute mind is perceptive and penetrating, showing deep understanding of a situation.

clue.text: Soho open-air boxing ring

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An outdoor boxing ring in Soho, London's nightlife district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing ring' looks like one phrase; 'boxing' is the hiding signal and 'ring' the definition. The answer sits across SoHO OPen-air.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular band of metal or wood, such as one rolled along or basketball's rim, is a circle.

clue.text: Pound piano after yank stops short

indicators.note: after tells us the piano letter comes behind the cut-short word
stops short means the word for yank loses its final letter

parts.note: to yank is to pull
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone thumps the piano after a sudden tug brings them to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops short' cuts PULL to PUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat something into a soft, mushy mass is to crush it, as in beating someone to a mash.

clue.text: Remit to embrace latitude and freedom of movement

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold, so the payment letters wrap around the latitude letter

parts.note: to remit money is to pay it

explanation.surface: A remit that allows some leeway and room to move.
explanation.walkthrough: Latitude itself means leeway, which suits the definition, but here it supplies only L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack in a mechanism, as in a rope with some give, is space for parts to move freely.

clue.text: A French designer with back to front means of communication

indicators.note: with back to front means the last letter is moved round to the start

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A French couturier with a garment on back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with back to front' moves the R at the end of ADIOR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless broadcasting by electromagnetic waves is a medium for sending messages and programmes.

clue.text: Example of accepted position

parts.note: in means accepted or fashionable, as in the in crowd
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: An example of a position that has become accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: A single case cited to illustrate something is a specimen or case in point.
